transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (HelioPay - Head of ML), Aisha Kaur (HelioPay - Platform), Tom Alvarez (HelioPay - Finance)

Summary:
Quick QBR-style checkpoint to review usage trends (Feb-Mar), cost drivers, recent reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment for H2. Discussed Dedicated pilot versus continuing on Hosted, cost-optimization levers (batching, prefix cache, quantization), and compliance questions for SOC2/SSO mapping. Agreed on follow-ups: detailed token-level export, latency bench, and scheduling deeper private-deploy feasibility review.

Topics (auto):
- Usage & spikes
- Token-level cost drivers
- Latency incidents & error budget
- Dedicated pilot ROI & timeline
- Security / compliance docs (SOC2 mapping)
- Roadmap alignment & next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Alright, everyone, thanks for joining. this is Maya from Redwood, and Liam is with me from SE. we scheduled 45 minutes so we'll try to keep tight.
[00:12] Rajiv: Cool, thanks. we are short on time, so high level then dig if needed.
[00:18] Liam: Quick agenda — usage trends, then cost, then reliability incidents I saw in the past month, and then options for a Dedicated pilot vs staying on Hosted.
[00:30] Tom: From Finance side, I mainly want to understand the drivers — why March costs jumped 28% vs Feb.
[00:38] Maya: Yep. we've pulled a 30-day token-level export, we'll send it after the call. initial read is two things: longer average generated lengths on receipts flows and an uptick in retries across one of your routes, which increases total tokens.
[00:55] Aisha: The receipts flow — we did enable more detailed line-item expansions in mid-Feb, that explains length. but retries — curious, retries where?
[01:05] Liam: The spikes map to the /inference/finex route — looks like timeout-triggered client-side retries at 2xx volumes around 03/14 to 03/19. Some of that is backpressure when the pods hit the KV cash — excuse me, KV cache — miss storms, so tail latency spikes and clients retry.
[01:25] Rajiv: KV cash, ha, I thought you said cash. yes. so is that on Hosted or Dedicated?
[01:30] Liam: That's on Hosted. Your tenant is on our standard hosted pool currently. we can tune batching and prefix caching to reduce misses; some short-term config, and longer-term option is Dedicated which isolates capacity and should reduce that contention.
[01:45] Tom: What kind of delta do we expect cost-wise for Dedicated? rough numbers are fine.
[01:50] Maya: Ballpark — with a Dedicated pilot sized for your 95th percentile traffic, your per-token cost can drop by ~18-30% depending on batching and quantization applied. but there is a base reserved cost component. so it's a tradeoff: predictable monthly commit + lower unit cost vs pay-as-you-go but higher variability.
[02:10] Rajiv: We need predictability more than lowest absolute cost. compliance teams also like isolation.
[02:16] Aisha: On isolation — if we move to Dedicated or Private, what about SSO and audit logs? we need SAML plus long-term audit retention.
[02:25] Liam: SSO via SAML is supported for Dedicated and Private; audit logs can be routed to your SIEM or S3 retention policies. we'll share the mapping doc, but short answer: yes, supported; there are add-ons for extended retention.
[02:39] Tom: Anything SOC2 specific? our infosec asked for the controls mapping.
[02:44] Maya: We'll drop the SOC2 mapping sheet after. it's the standard one we share with enterprise.
[02:48] Rajiv: On reliability, you mentioned incidents — can you walk through the March 18th incident?
[02:55] Liam: Sure. on 03/18 there was a region-level capacity pressure in us-west-2 during the 17:00 peak, some models experienced elevated queue times. Automatic routing shifted some requests to secondary hosts but there was a brief window (~6 minutes) where error rates rose to 3.2%. We have a post-incident note; the root cause was a mis-sized autoscale config combined with a new model kernel causing higher memory usage. we've patched autoscaler thresholds and released a kernel fallback.
[03:26] Aisha: Did we see any data loss?
[03:28] Liam: No data loss — only transient 5xx returns while requests retried. Most client retries succeeded afterwards but cumulatively that produced retry storms which added to cost.
[03:38] Tom: So from finance POV, that tail of retries contributed to the cost spike. makes sense.
[03:43] Maya: Correct. on the optimization side there are quick wins: 1) prefix/KV caching for stable prompts; 2) conservative client-side retry backoff recommendations; 3) enable batching windows for the route where latency budgets allow; 4) quantization recommendation for some model variants.
[04:05] Rajiv: Quantization — any quality regression risk? we ran some A/B tests earlier and saw slight BLEU-ish style regressions for hallucination-prone flows.
[04:15] Liam: For generation in receipts the tolerance is higher; but for high-stakes regulatory text we recommend a canary: run a small portion on quantized model variant and run your eval sets. Redwood Optimize will suggest which layers and bit widths consider safe. we'll help set up the canary.
[04:35] Aisha: OK. about the Dedicated pilot — timeline? we want something in April if possible.
[04:40] Maya: We can stand up a small Dedicated pool as a pilot in 2-3 weeks, depending on commitment paperwork. minimal path is 1-month commit to validate. if you want leap to Private it'll take longer.
[04:54] Tom: Paperwork — procurement is slower. can we get estimates before procurement?
[04:58] Maya: Yes we'll send an estimated monthly committed cost and an amortized unit cost model.
[05:05] Rajiv: For the benchmark, can you run a 4k context latency bench? our receipts occasionally go long when we include full conversation history.
[05:13] Liam: Yup, Liam: I'll run a 95th percentile latency bench on Dedicated with 4k context and share logs. note I'll include both streaming and non-streaming paths.
[05:23] Rajiv: Great. also, can we set a per-route SLO? like 200ms p95 for simple classification and 1.5s p95 for long-gen?
[05:31] Aisha: We need formal SLOs for the contract.
[05:34] Maya: We can put a proposed SLO matrix in the pilot proposal.
[05:38] Tom: Back to costs, any immediate config we can flip to reduce March-like surges?
[05:43] Liam: Turn on prefix cache for receipts, adjust client retry backoffs, and add conservative batching windows of 50–100ms where acceptable — that'll bite on a little latency for some requests but reduce per-token unit cost.
[05:56] Rajiv: Is there any risk to analytics accuracy if we buffer/batch? we have threaded per-event attribution that relies on timestamps.
[06:03] Liam: Batching is transparent at the API layer — you'll still get per-request response IDs and timestamps. we can preserve attribution; we just coalesce compute.
[06:12] Maya: Quick note: there are also model variants with lower cost per token — we have some open-source quantized checkpoints we verified for financial text. not identical output but often acceptable.
[06:24] Aisha: Can you share the evaluation reports for the quantized variants?
[06:28] Liam: Yes, I'll attach the Redwood Optimize eval output and suggested prompt sets.
[06:33] [07:00] (brief side conversation about calendar invites, minor crosstalk, omitted)
[07:15] Tom: On forecasting — if we did Dedicated, would we still be billed for overflow on Hosted? how does overflow routing work?
[07:22] Maya: You can configure overflow/fallback policies. typical pattern: Dedicated handles baseline and we'll route overflow to Hosted with priority routing — that prevents dropped traffic but costs per token on Hosted. We can also reserve burst capacity to minimize overflow billing surprises.
[07:40] Rajiv: For compliance, we also need KMS integration for keys if we do Private. how is KMS handled for Dedicated?
[07:47] Liam: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS keys for model encryption at rest and you can also bring your own HSM for Private. We'll share the KMS integration spec.
[07:56] Aisha: On audit logs, we might want 12 months retention. is that an add-on?
[07:59] Maya: Extended retention is an add-on; we'll include pricing in the doc.
[08:05] Rajiv: Any other reliability mitigations besides autoscaler tuning?
[08:09] Liam: Kernel selection fallback, proactive kernel testing on canary traffic, and improved autoscale thresholds. also hot-key detection to avoid skewed batching.
[08:18] Aisha: About hot keys — we saw one customer id that was producing heavy traffic, is there a way to throttle or isolate?
[08:24] Liam: You can set per-route quotas and per-token rate limits, and we have route-level isolation on Dedicated.
[08:31] Tom: Ok, sounds good. from finance I just need the amortized model and expected month-to-month with a 3-month pilot.
[08:38] Maya: We'll provide three scenarios: conservative (no quantization, small batching), optimized (batching + prefix cache), and aggressive (quant + high batching).
[08:48] Rajiv: For the deep-dive, can we include architecture for Private (VPC, on-prem) because legal is pushing for air-gapped for some customers.
[08:56] Maya: Absolutely. Private takes longer — we estimate 8–12 weeks for fully private on-prem; VPC-hosted private is faster. we'll outline options.
[09:06] Aisha: Anything about data residency? we need EU-only for some segments.
[09:10] Liam: We support region pinning for customer objects and data residency in EU regions, yes.
[09:15] (noise)
[09:20] Tom: Quick question — competitors. our security said Anthropic is pitching a private endpoint — any notes?
[09:27] Maya: Anthropic often focuses on model safety; they'd push private endpoints too. OpenAI has hosted with enterprise features. Cohere similar with dedicated endpoints. We'll share a short competitive note.
[09:37] Rajiv: Can you recap next steps?
[09:40] Maya: Sure — recap: 1) Maya sends 30-day token-level breakdown and optimization suggestions by Apr 2. 2) Liam runs p95 latency bench on Dedicated with 4k context and shares artifacts by Apr 6. 3) HelioPay (Aisha) provides peak inference windows and SLO targets by Mar 31. 4) Finance (Tom) confirms budget band for 1-month Dedicated pilot by Apr 8. 5) Schedule technical deep-dive for Private feasibility week of Apr 6.
[10:12] Tom: That works, thanks.
[10:15] Rajiv: Quick note — please flag any config that would require SDK changes, we prefer zero client changes.
[10:22] Liam: Most batching and cache flips are server-side and transparent, we'll call out any client-side backoff recommendations.
[10:30] Maya: Alright, thanks all — we'll follow up with notes and the docs.
[10:35] End of meeting.

Files shared during call (links):
- 30-day token export (will be shared after call)
- SOC2 controls mapping (link to doc)
- Redwood Optimize quantization summary (link to doc)

Call notes / quick hits:
- Root cause for Mar 18 incident: autoscale thresholds + model kernel memory spike; fixed with autoscale patch and kernel fallback.
- Immediate quick wins: enable prefix cache for receipts, adjust retry backoff policy, add short batching window where latency tolerates.
- Pilot suggestion: 1-month Dedicated pilot to validate predictability; conservative + optimized + aggressive scenario costing to be provided.

End transcript.
